description:
All eight use-case wrappers (verify_tls_server, verify_tls_client_dns, verify_tls_client_mailbox, verify_smime_signer, verify_smime_recipient, verify_code_signer, verify_time_stamper, verify_ocsp_responder) bake `&NoAiaFetcher` internally (lines 770, 855, 932, 1001, 1034, 1085, 1155, 1288). The only way to wire an AiaFetcher into a TLS-server-validation call is to abandon the wrapper and reimplement the path-build + identity-binding + post-validation-EKU/KU/delegation glue by hand on top of verify_chain.

SCENARIO that triggers cost: a deployer wants AIA chain reassembly for TLS server validation (the original motivation for adding AIA fetching). They write `verify_tls_server(&[leaf_only], &anchors, &name, &profile, now, &NoRevocation)` and get Error::Aia(FetchingDisabled). They look at the wrapper signature, find no fetcher arg, look at the docs, find 'Callers that want AIA fetching must drop down to verify_chain or construct a Verifier directly.' They now have to re-implement:

- verify_tls_server: the verify_dns_name post-call on chain[0]
- verify_smime_signer/recipient: the verify_mailbox post-call
- verify_time_stamper: the enforce_timestamping_eku_critical_and_sole + enforce_timestamping_ku_shape post-calls (these are PRIVATE — they have no public API)
- verify_ocsp_responder: the has_ocsp_no_check check, NoCheckShim construction, verify_responder_is_delegated_by post-call (also PRIVATE)

So 'drop down to verify_chain' is not actually a feasible escape hatch for the time-stamper and OCSP-responder wrappers because their post-validation logic is private. A caller wanting AIA + TSA validation literally cannot achieve it without forking pkix-chain.

MAINTENANCE CONSEQUENCE: Every user with a non-trivial PKI hits this. They open an issue 'verify_tls_server doesn't fetch AIA, why bother adding AIA at all?' You then have to either (a) ship eight more wrappers with an extra fetcher arg, doubling the surface; (b) make the existing wrappers generic over A: AiaFetcher with a default of NoAiaFetcher; (c) make the post-validation helpers (enforce_timestamping_eku_critical_and_sole, etc.) pub. All three are API-additive but commit you to the shape.

The 1.0 CHANGELOG already commits to 'wrappers bake NoAiaFetcher; signatures unchanged.' Picking (b) now (generic with default) preserves the call-site shape AND admits AIA without a future breaking change. Picking (a) or (c) requires breaking changes or doubling the wrapper count later. This is exactly the kind of API-locked-in decision that needs to be made before 1.0, per AGENTS.md's 'Project phase and decision framing' guidance.

RECOMMENDATION: before 1.0 ships, make the wrappers generic over A: AiaFetcher = NoAiaFetcher (matching Verifier's shape). The default behavior is preserved; the upgrade path is open without a 2.0.
title: use-case wrappers silently disable AIA fetching; no opt-in path short of dropping to verify_chain
